questions.prompt: Page one filters tenant east and active documents. What belongs on page two?

options.label: Keep the authorization and document predicate on every page request.
Only the user-supplied cursor; it replaces the tenant predicate.
Any tenant the cursor names, since it is a continuation token.

questions.explanation: A continuation cursor is untrusted input and does not grant authority. Preserve current authorization and the intended document predicate on every request, with the chosen consistency policy.

questions.prompt: Ascending score/id pagination ended at (2,b). How should the next page resume?

options.label: Use score >= 2 alone, which can repeat earlier results.
Use score > 2 alone, which can drop later ties.
Order by score and a unique tie-breaker, then resume strictly after the full cursor tuple.

questions.explanation: The complete tuple predicate distinguishes later score-2 identities from already returned ties. Combine strict tuple continuation with the original permission/filter; a unique tie-breaker fixes order.

questions.prompt: A later page uses an increasingly large skip offset. What work should be reviewed?

options.label: Range pagination makes authorization and index checks unnecessary.
Growing skip offsets require scanning past earlier results; compare an indexed range query.
Skip has the same fixed cost regardless of offset and index.

questions.explanation: The server must pass earlier results for skip pagination. A suitable indexed range query can avoid unwanted scans, but its actual predicate, sort and workload still need plan evidence.

questions.prompt: Two plans have an index name and return two documents. Which evidence supports their work comparison?

options.label: Inspect the plan and examined-versus-returned work under representative data; an index name alone proves no deadline.
The index name alone guarantees a deadline for every tenant.
Only the two returned rows matter; examined work is irrelevant.

questions.explanation: Compare examined documents/keys, returned results, sort/fetch stages and representative data/load. An index label is not a latency guarantee, and an isolated explain run is not a production benchmark.

questions.prompt: A lower-scored document is inserted after the first cursor page. What has the cursor established?

options.label: An immutable collection snapshot across all page requests.
A guarantee that every concurrent insert appears exactly once.
A cursor is a continuation rule, not a guarantee of an unchanged concurrent result set.

questions.explanation: The cursor defines where the next query continues. Concurrent inserts and sort-key changes can change membership; stable-snapshot, changing-feed or explicit-refresh behavior must be defined separately.
